finding.claim: Stored subscriber callback URL is fetched server-side with no validation, so a subscriber can make the server send POST requests to arbitrary internal or external http(s) targets, on a schedule.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13), documented as coming from POST /subscribe
finding.sink: URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21, then client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe with body fields name and callbackUrl.
subscribe(name, callbackUrl) takes the attacker-supplied URL as a raw String.
Stored unchanged into the static subscriptions map. No scheme, host, or address check.
notifyAll runs every minute, so the sink fires without further attacker action.
Iterates over every stored callback URL.
URI.create(cb) builds the request target directly from the stored value.
POST with the payload body. The payload comes from the caller of notifyAll, not from the subscriber.
client.send issues the request from the server. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. subscribe() does no validation (line 14). notifyAll() does no validation (lines 19-23). The default HttpClient (line 10) does not follow redirects, so redirect-based escape does not apply, but that does not stop a direct request to an internal host. Java's HttpClient only accepts http and https schemes, which limits scheme abuse (file:, gopher:) but not internal http targets such as 169.254.169.254, localhost, or RFC1918 addresses. Access control on the POST /subscribe route is not in this repo, so I could not confirm whether it is authenticated. If it is open to unauthenticated users, the finding is more severe.

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe() stores callbackUrl unchanged (src/Jobs.java:14). notifyAll() passes it straight to URI.create (src/Jobs.java:21) and client.send (src/Jobs.java:24) with no scheme, host, or address check. The only validation in the file is in thumb() (src/Jobs.java:30), which is a different function and does not run on this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: subscribe() stores the raw callbackUrl at src/Jobs.java:14, and notifyAll() sends a POST to it at src/Jobs.java:21-24 with no check. The source is a subscriber-supplied value (documented POST /subscribe at src/Jobs.java:12), so a low-privilege user can reach the sink. Caveats: the POST /subscribe route, its auth, and the once-a-minute scheduler are not in this repo (line 17 is only a comment), so exploitability depends on those being open to low-privilege users.
